I reviewed the uncommitted changes in `lib/` and reported four findings. I only read the diff and `shouldBypassProxy.js`. I didn't run any code or read the modified test files.

1. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:132`:** The old `assertValidHeaderValue` check threw on CR/LF in header values. It is gone, and the new code silently strips those characters. A value like `'a\r\nInjected: 1'` now goes out as `aInjected: 1` with no error, which hides injection attempts.
2. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:8`:** The new regex deletes every character above U+00FF and most control characters. A header value in Japanese or with an emoji is silently truncated or emptied.
3. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:42`:** `normalizeValue` now trims leading and trailing spaces and tabs from every header value. This can break values that depend on exact whitespace, such as signed or hashed headers.
4. **`lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js:108`:** Any loopback name now matches any other loopback name. `NO_PROXY=localhost` also bypasses the proxy for `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`, which breaks setups that proxy one loopback address on purpose. The alias check only covers `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, so other loopback forms such as `127.0.0.2` are still treated differently.

I haven't confirmed the third finding against the modified tests.

findings.summary: The new sanitizer silently strips CR/LF and other control characters from header values. The `assertValidHeaderValue` check that threw on CR/LF was removed.
findings.failure_scenario: `headers.set('X-Foo', 'a\r\nInjected: 1')` used to throw. It now stores `aInjected: 1` and sends it. Code that relies on the rejection no longer gets it. Corrupted or attacker-influenced values go out on the wire with no error, which hides injection attempts instead of surfacing them.

findings.summary: `INVALID_HEADER_VALUE_CHARS_RE` (`/[^\x09\x20-\x7E\x80-\xFF]/g`) deletes every character above U+00FF, plus 0x00-0x08, 0x0B-0x1F and 0x7F.
findings.failure_scenario: A header value such as `X-Name: 日本語` or one containing an emoji, for example a Content-Disposition filename or a custom metadata header, silently loses those characters. The result is an empty or truncated value with no error. Previously the value passed through and Node raised its own error.

findings.summary: `normalizeValue` now trims leading and trailing spaces and tabs on every header value. Before, it only stripped trailing CR/LF.
findings.failure_scenario: A value that intentionally has leading or trailing whitespace is changed. Examples are a signed or hashed header value, or a `Content-Type` parameter. Signatures computed over the original string no longer match what is sent.

findings.summary: Loopback aliases are now treated as equivalent. Any loopback `NO_PROXY` entry bypasses the proxy for every loopback hostname, which ignores the port semantics and exact-match rules for the other entries.
findings.failure_scenario: With `NO_PROXY=localhost`, a request to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` or `http://[::1]/` now bypasses the proxy, though the user only listed `localhost`. Setups that deliberately proxy `127.0.0.1` (for example, an SSH tunnel to a remote service) while excluding `localhost` break. The `::1` entry also never matches a bracketed hostname through the loopback check unless `normalizeNoProxyHost` strips the brackets first. Other loopback forms such as `127.0.0.2` and `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1` are not covered, so the alias behavior is inconsistent.
